title: Keel runs live Allocation Instances while their RRC Framework implementation coverage is still Pending
content:
The first field of every Instance Configuration Document is **RRC Framework Full Implementation Coverage**, and in all five Instances in this chunk its value is `Pending`: Kamino PYUSD (A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.3.1.1.5.1), Drift USDS (A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.3.1.2.1.1), Drift USDC (A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.3.1.2.2.1), Drift USDT (A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.3.1.2.3.1) and Drift PYUSD (A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.3.1.2.4.1).

These documents sit under **Active Instances** — the branch reserved for "Instances of the Keel Liquidity Layer with `Active` Status". So the Atlas simultaneously records that these conduits are live and that their risk-framework coverage is incomplete.

The tension is worth stating plainly rather than resolving: either full RRC coverage is a precondition for deployment, in which case these Instances are out of compliance, or it is not, in which case the field documents an aspiration rather than a gate. The Atlas's own structure — putting the field *first*, above parameters — suggests it is meant to be read as a gate.

What makes the observation useful is that the deficiency is disclosed uniformly and machine-readably. The pending status is not hidden in prose; it is a named field with a consistent value, which means the gap between deployed exposure and completed risk coverage is measurable at any time.
description: Every Instance Configuration Document in the Active Instances branch marks RRC Framework Full Implementation Coverage as `Pending`, so capital is deployed ahead of complete risk-framework coverage.
